  the scores
  SPY · historical data timeout for SPY after 45s: context deadline exceeded ·
    failed 5 Sep 13:00 · next try 5 Sep 15:00 · 530 sessions kept
  SYNC · contract details unresolved for SYNC: no security definition has been
    found · failed 5 Sep 11:00 · next try 5 Sep 19:00 · no history

Reading · z is the underlying's move from the close of the fill's session, net
  of its exposure to the market and, where the name has one, to its sector fund,
  in units of its own daily noise; positive means the move went the decision's
  way. On an index (SPY, SPX, QQQ and the like, or a name that moves with SPY at
  R² 0.90 or more) z is the index's whole move in units of its whole daily
  noise. Entries (opens and adds) carry the gates; exits (trims and exits) and
  the index streams are reported, never gated. One name in one entry week is one
  unit of evidence; units whose horizons overlap count less, so the effective
  sample is smaller than the unit count. The directional score is the mean z per
  unit; it is not a correlation. The e-value is the weight of evidence for
  information in the decisions (20 is the bar); the posterior gives the chance
  the true score exceeds 0, 0.05 and 0.10; the futility e-value weighs no
  information against a score of 0.05, the smallest worth a risk allocation.
A sleeve is established only when every gate on its entries passes, the
  sign-shuffle placebo included; until then nothing here says whether the
  decisions carry information. Slippage is the half-spread paid against the
  quote retained at the fill; fills before 18 Oct 2026 have none. Fills made by
  Canary's rules or the broker's lifecycle are the rule sleeve and count for no
  one. Read-only review of past fills; it places no orders.
